h1: The 7 Best eGPU Enclosures for an RTX 3080, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: eGPU Enclosures for RTX 3080: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 7 eGPU enclosures that can host an RTX 3080, scored on power supply, card clearance, Thunderbolt generation and laptop charging.
summary: The ORARA 750W enclosure is the best eGPU box for an RTX 3080, with a built-in 750W supply, a Thunderbolt 3/4/USB4 controller and room for most two-slot cards. The Sonnet Breakaway Box 750 is the proven Mac and Windows alternative, the Plugable Thunderbolt 5 box is the future-proof choice, and the open-frame Maskedfish suits oversized cards.
intro: An RTX 3080 is a 320 watt class card, and that single number rules out half the eGPU enclosures on the market. Small boxes with 240W supplies are designed for low-power cards, and they cannot feed a 3080 without brownouts or shutdowns. Before comparing speeds, check that the power supply can hand over the card's draw with margin to spare.

Seven enclosures are ranked here for an RTX 3080 build. The list covers boxes with their own supply, open frames that take an ATX power supply, and a Thunderbolt 5 model. Each is scored on supply wattage, card clearance, controller and port generation, and laptop charging. A 240W box was excluded for this reason: it cannot power the card.

products.name: ORARA eGPU Enclosure Thunderbolt 3/4/USB4 40Gbps with 750W PSU
products.verdict: A 750W supply, a JHL7440 controller and clearance for 13.7 inch cards that are not triple-slot.
products.description:
The ORARA includes a 750W power supply, uses a JHL7440 Thunderbolt controller with a 32Gbps daisy chain, and works over Thunderbolt 3, 4 and USB4 at 40Gbps. It fits cards up to 13.7 by 6.17 by 2.3 inches and no triple-slot designs.

A 750W supply gives a 3080 plenty of room, since the card draws around 320W and a CPU-less enclosure has little else to power. It ranks first because the all-in-one box removes the guesswork of picking a supply and a case. The clearance limit is the catch: many partner 3080s are three slots thick, so measure your card before ordering.

Buy it if your 3080 is a two-slot card and you want a self-contained box. Skip it if your card is a chunky triple-slot design.
products.idealFor: Two-slot RTX 3080 cards on a Thunderbolt laptop.

products.name: Sonnet eGPU Breakaway Box 750, External GPU Chassis
products.verdict: A 750W Thunderbolt 3 chassis for Mac and Windows with a variable-speed, temperature-controlled fan.
products.description:
The Sonnet Breakaway Box 750 offers a 750W supply, Thunderbolt 3 connectivity, Mac and Windows compatibility, and a variable-speed fan controlled by temperature. The listing describes the sizing as future-proof.

Sonnet has made Breakaway Boxes for years, so the compatibility notes and community experience around it are deep, which counts for a product that depends on driver and firmware quirks. It ranks second to the ORARA because the connection is Thunderbolt 3 only in the listing, and the data omits clearance details.

Buy it if you want a long-established brand and a quiet fan. Skip it if you need Thunderbolt 4 or USB4 features.
products.idealFor: Mac users and anyone wanting proven support.

products.name: Plugable Thunderbolt 5 AI eGPU Enclosure & Dock, 850W PSU (TBT5-AI)
products.verdict: An 850W 80+ Gold supply, 80Gbps Thunderbolt 5 and room for 3.5 slot cards.
products.description:
The Plugable TBT5-AI has an 850W 80+ Gold supply with 600W dedicated to the GPU, 80Gbps Thunderbolt 5, 2.5Gbps Ethernet and room for a card up to 346 by 170 by 77mm, or 3.5 slots.

It fits a triple-slot RTX 3080 where the ORARA cannot, and Thunderbolt 5 gives headroom for later cards. The rub is that a 3080 will not use the extra bandwidth on a Thunderbolt 3 or 4 laptop, and you pay for the new port generation regardless. It lands third because the premium buys features beyond what a 3080 needs.

Buy it if you have a triple-slot 3080 or plan to upgrade the GPU. Skip it if you only want to run a 3080 on an older laptop.
cons: Extra bandwidth unused on older laptops
products.skipIf: You have an older Thunderbolt laptop.

products.name: Sonnet Breakaway Box 850 T5 eGPU Enclosure, 80Gbps Thunderbolt 5
products.verdict: An 850W supply with triple-wide card support, 80Gbps, a 5GbE port and three USB-A dock ports.
products.description:
The Breakaway Box 850 T5 has an 850W supply, supports triple-wide cards and offers 80Gbps bidirectional Thunderbolt 5, a 5GbE port and 3 USB-A 10Gbps ports.

It competes with the Plugable on nearly every spec, and the dock ports are the difference: a 5GbE socket and three fast USB-A ports turn the box into a docking station. It ranks fourth because the listing gives no detail on the GPU-dedicated wattage, which the Plugable states.

Buy it if you want the box to double as a dock. Skip it if the Plugable's published GPU wattage appeals more.
products.idealFor: A 3080 box that doubles as a dock.

products.name: Maskedfish eGPU Enclosure Thunderbolt 3/4 USB4 40Gbps PD 85W Charging (MK-L18)
products.verdict: An open frame with PCIe 4.0 x16 mode, 85W laptop charging and no GPU length limit.
products.description:
The Maskedfish MK-L18 uses JHL7540 or JHL7440 controllers with PCIe 4.0 x16 mode, offers 85W power delivery charging and dual Thunderbolt ports, and its open frame places no limit on GPU length.

It suits cards that will not fit sealed boxes, including long or triple-slot 3080s. The listing we reviewed does not list a power supply, so assume you provide an ATX unit of at least 750W and wire it yourself. The 85W laptop charging is welcome if the host has a Thunderbolt power-in.

Buy it if your card is large and you are comfortable with an open build. Skip it if you want a plug-and-play box.
products.skipIf: You want a sealed, plug-in box.

products.name: VIKINYEE Thunderbolt 3/4 eGPU Enclosure USB4 (VK-Y900)
products.verdict: A JHL7440/7450 controller board with ENIG plating and dual Thunderbolt ports with 85W charging.
products.description:
The VIKINYEE VK-Y900 uses JHL7440 or JHL7450 controllers on an ENIG-plated PCB, with dual Thunderbolt ports (15W and 85W PD) and support for RTX 50-series and RX 9000-series cards.

ENIG plating is a gold-over-nickel finish that resists corrosion on the board's contacts. It ranks sixth because the listing gives no power supply and no clearance, so a 3080 fit depends on your own supply and case. The 85W port helps keep a laptop alive.

Buy it if you want a well-built controller board and a flexible build. Skip it if you want a sealed box.
products.idealFor: DIY builders with their own supply.

products.name: External GPU Dock Station, Mini eGPU Enclosure Thunderbolt 3/4 USB4 40Gbps
products.verdict: A mini dock that accepts ATX, SFX, FLEX or DC 12V power and doubles as a USB-A and TB4 hub.
products.description:
This mini eGPU dock works with ATX, SFX, FLEX or DC 12V power, uses a JHL7440 controller with a 32Gbps daisy chain, and doubles as a USB-A and Thunderbolt 4 hub.

Power flexibility is the draw: an SFX supply keeps the build compact, and an ATX supply gives a 3080 all it needs. It ranks last because it ships without a case or supply, so the result depends on what you pair it with, and the listing details nothing about card clearance.

Buy it if you already own a suitable power supply. Skip it if you want a finished enclosure.
products.idealFor: Builders reusing a spare power supply.

whatMatters.detail: An RTX 3080 draws around 320W, plus headroom for spikes. A 750W supply gives comfortable margin, while a 240W box cannot run the card. Confirm the supply wattage in the listing.

Partner 3080s vary: some are two-slot, many are triple-slot, and lengths range widely. Check the enclosure's maximum card size, such as 13.7 inches and no triple-slot on the ORARA, and compare with your card's spec.

A 40Gbps link carries less data than the PCIe slot a 3080 normally uses, so some performance is lost. Thunderbolt 5 doubles the link to 80Gbps if your laptop supports it. Older laptops cannot take advantage.
A port with 85W power delivery can charge a thin laptop while it games, leaving one cable on the desk. Lower wattages only trickle charge. Check the PD figure.
Open frames accept any card length and run cooler, but expose the card to dust. Sealed boxes look tidy and are quieter. Choose by your card and your desk.

faq.q: Can an eGPU run an RTX 3080 well?
faq.a: Yes, but over Thunderbolt 3 or 4 the 40Gbps link caps throughput, so you will see less performance than in a desktop. Thunderbolt 5 improves it on supported hosts.

faq.q: What is the biggest mistake when buying an eGPU enclosure?
faq.a: Overlooking the power supply. A 240W box cannot run a 320W card. Make sure the supply is at least 750W.

faq.q: Is the Plugable worth it over the ORARA?
faq.a: Only for a triple-slot card or a Thunderbolt 5 host. Otherwise, the ORARA gives the same 3080 headroom for less.
Yes, a Thunderbolt 3, 4 or 5 port, or USB4 on supported machines. A plain USB-C port will not work.

faq.q: Can I use it with a Mac?
faq.a: Recent Apple silicon Macs do not support external GPUs for graphics. Older Intel Macs with Thunderbolt 3 do, which is the audience for the Sonnet 750.
Sealed boxes rely on their fans, and open frames rely on room airflow. Keep vents clear and avoid enclosed shelves.

finalTake: For a two-slot RTX 3080, the ORARA eGPU enclosure is the best choice, with a 750W supply, a Thunderbolt 3/4/USB4 controller and a self-contained design. The Sonnet 750 is the proven alternative for Macs, the Plugable Thunderbolt 5 is the choice for triple-slot cards, and the Maskedfish open frame handles anything. Check the card's thickness and your laptop's port before you order.
